category: Vertical SaaS / SMB unit economics (restaurant-retail POS)
stage: Growth (Series A vertical SaaS, ~8,000 paying outlets)
title: Pune restaurant-POS halved CAC payback (14→8.5 months) by replacing paid acquisition with WhatsApp vernacular onboarding and a login-triggered save-desk
content: A Pune-HQ restaurant-and-retail POS sold to thin-margin SMBs at ₹1,499/month ARPU (~45% gross margin, so ~₹675/month recovered per outlet). Blended CAC on Meta + Google had crept to ₹9,200, putting payback at ~14 months. Worse, Month-3 logo churn was 7.2%/month — mostly tier-2/3 single-outlet owners in Indore, Surat and Nagpur who never finished setup. We were buying customers who quit before they paid back acquisition. So we attacked CAC and churn as one problem. We cut Meta prospecting 40% and moved that budget to Justdial intent leads plus a Click-to-WhatsApp demo campaign; a vernacular WhatsApp flow (Hindi/Gujarati voice notes + a 6-step setup video) replaced the call-centre handoff. Then a save-desk: any outlet with under 3 logins in 14 days got a WhatsApp nudge and a free done-for-you menu upload. Over 5 months CTWA cut CAC to ₹5,600 (-39%), 7-day activation (first bill printed) rose 54%→81%, and Month-3 churn fell 7.2%→3.9%. Payback dropped 14→8.5 months on gross margin; LTV:CAC moved 1.8x→3.1x.
lesson: For thin-margin SMB SaaS, CAC and churn are the same equation — you cannot out-spend broken activation. Fix the first 14 days in the customer's own language before you buy a single new lead: a vernacular WhatsApp onboarding flow plus a login-triggered save-desk beats any ad-creative optimisation, because an outlet that prints its first bill is an outlet that pays back.
